open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token;
open_points.question: Are these three HTTP operations exceptions to A5 rule 1, which says every operation except the health answer requires exactly one Authorization field, or must they require the token?
options: Treat the documentation operations as additional explicit exceptions and serve them without authentication
Apply A5 rule 1 and answer unauthenticated documentation requests with the UNAUTHORIZED M08 response
Declare that documentation endpoints are not operations for purposes of A5 and state that scope explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Treat the three documentation endpoints as explicit unauthenticated exceptions and amend A5 accordingly.

witness.initial: The service is listening and its documentation endpoints are enabled.
events: A caller sends GET /openapi.json without an Authorization field.
outcomes: The changed State 5 passage returns the generated description without a token.
A5 rule 1 refuses the request with the UNAUTHORIZED M08 response before examining anything else.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text: A path that is not a route answers 404,
open_points.question: What exact path matching and normalization determine whether a request is a route, including a trailing slash, repeated slash, percent-encoded segment or other framework-normalized spelling?
options: Match only the literal declared paths and answer every other spelling with 404
Use the framework's normalization and automatic slash redirects
List the permitted equivalent spellings and the response for each
open_points.default_guess: Disable automatic slash redirects and match only the literal declared paths.

witness.initial: The service is listening with the declared GET /health route.
outcomes: The path is not the literal route and answers 404.
The framework recognizes a slash variant and redirects the caller to /health.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token;
open_points.question: Which HTTP methods are supported at each documentation path, and what must unsupported methods answer?
options: Support GET only and answer every other method with 405
Support GET and HEAD
Leave method handling entirely to the selected framework
open_points.default_guess: Support GET only and answer other methods with the framework's 405 response.

witness.initial: The service is listening and /openapi.json is enabled.
events: A caller sends HEAD /openapi.json without a token.
outcomes: The endpoint answers 200 with the headers of the generated OpenAPI document and no response body.
The endpoint supports only GET and answers 405.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token;
open_points.question: What representation, status and media type must each of /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json return, rather than merely saying that each serves the generated description?
options: Serve Swagger UI HTML at /docs, ReDoc HTML at /redoc and an OpenAPI JSON document at /openapi.json
Serve the same machine-readable description at all three paths
Use whatever representations and content types the framework version supplies
open_points.default_guess: Use the framework defaults: Swagger UI HTML, ReDoc HTML and OpenAPI JSON respectively.

witness.initial: The service is listening with documentation enabled.
outcomes: The caller receives an HTML documentation application.
The caller receives the machine-readable generated description directly.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text:
it names the routes and the forms of their bodies and
answers,
open_points.question: Must the generated description declare the required Authorization header or bearer security scheme for scan, delivery and mark, and the absence of that requirement for health and documentation?
options: Declare a bearer security scheme on the three protected routes and no scheme on health or documentation
Describe only paths, bodies and responses, omitting authentication because handlers check it manually
Declare Authorization as an ordinary required header parameter on each protected route
open_points.default_guess: Declare a bearer security scheme on scan, delivery and mark, with health and documentation unauthenticated.

witness.initial: The service is listening and exposes its generated description.
events: A tool reads /openapi.json and generates a client for the scan route.
The generated client invokes the scan route without separately supplied undocumented behavior.
outcomes: The description declares authentication, so the client exposes a token input and sends Authorization.
The description omits authentication, so the generated client sends no Authorization field and receives an unauthorized refusal.
witness.observer: The client developer and the HTTP caller

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text:
it names the routes and the forms of their bodies and
answers,
open_points.question: Which answers must the generated description enumerate: only successful answers, every M08 status and schema, per-photo failed M06 outcomes, and/or framework 404 and 405 responses?
options: Describe every success and domain refusal or failure reachable from each route, plus applicable framework errors
Describe success models and M08 responses but leave framework errors implicit
Describe only successful response models and let undocumented errors occur at runtime
open_points.default_guess: Describe every success response and every route-specific M08 or M06/M07 outcome, while documenting the common framework 404 and 405 responses separately.

witness.initial: The service is listening and exposes /openapi.json.
events: A caller reads the delivery operation from /openapi.json.
The caller compares the documented responses with a delivery request whose project is unknown.
outcomes: The generated description includes the 404 M08 Refusal form for unknown_project.
The generated description lists only the successful M06 response even though the runtime returns an M08 refusal.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app
open_points.text:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token;
open_points.question: Must the /docs and /redoc pages be self-contained or locally served, or may their HTML load scripts, styles or fonts from third-party origins?
options: Bundle or serve every documentation asset locally
Permit the framework's default third-party asset URLs
Do not provide interactive HTML and expose only the machine-readable document
open_points.default_guess: Serve all documentation assets locally so opening the pages requires no third-party request.

witness.initial: The service is reachable from a browser that cannot access the public internet.
outcomes: The locally served documentation UI loads and is usable.
The HTML loads, but its externally hosted scripts or styles fail and the documentation UI is unusable.
